title: GovEagle vs Procurement Sciences (Awarded AI): Which Is Better for Federal Proposals?
summary: GovEagle vs. Awarded AI by Procurement Sciences, side by side: opportunity search, capture, proposals, Office add-ins, CRM, SharePoint, and security.
body_markdown:
GovEagle and Awarded AI by Procurement Sciences both serve government contractors across business development, capture, and proposals. On a feature list they look alike, so we compared them the way a pursuit actually runs: finding the opportunity, deciding whether to chase it, writing and pricing the proposal, and doing all of that inside the tools your team already uses. Here's what we found.


*This comparison was created using publicly available vendor materials reviewed on September 28, 2026. It describes documented capabilities and questions to verify in a demo, not a hands-on evaluation of Awarded AI. Products and deployment options change. Confirm current functionality and terms with each vendor.*


## GovEagle vs. Procurement Sciences (Awarded AI) at a glance


GovEagle Awarded AI by Procurement Sciences


**Opportunity search** Daily bid agents that qualify and score opportunities Bid search, smart matching, and bid/no-bid analysis


**Capture** Built-in capture exercises, gate reviews, and Price-to-Win Research agents, fit assessments, and gate reviews


**Proposals** RFP shredding, compliance, drafting, and color reviews Research, compliance checks, drafting, and Red Team reviews


**Microsoft Office** Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins Word add-in


**CRM** Integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Technomile Built-in CRM; Salesforce integration


**SharePoint** Sync with inherited permissions Sync of selected sites and folders


**DoD solicitations in PIEE** Included in daily opportunity search Unknown


**Template-filling workflows** Fills in your own Word, PowerPoint, and Excel templates Unknown


**Microsoft Teams** Channel conversations saved to opportunities Unknown


**Security** FedRAMP Certified (Moderate) FedRAMP Moderate authorization


**Deployment** SaaS, your own GovCloud, or air-gapped Single-tenant Azure, GovCloud, or self-hosted


*"Unknown" means we couldn't find the capability described in Procurement Sciences' public materials as of September 28, 2026. It doesn't mean Awarded AI lacks it; ask in the demo.*


The short version: both platforms cover the full pursuit. The differences are in how opportunities get qualified, how capture is structured, and how much of the work happens inside Office and your existing CRM.


## Opportunity search: who does the first pass?


Procurement Sciences' AI platform, Awarded AI, offers bid search, smart matching, natural-language search, and bid/no-bid analysis. Procurement Sciences also acquired HigherGov in May 2026, adding an established market-intelligence product to its portfolio. HigherGov still operates as its own product, so ask which data and workflows live in Awarded AI and which require a HigherGov subscription.


GovEagle[tracks and qualifies opportunities](https://www.goveagle.com/platform) with bid agents that run daily against[SAM.gov, GSA eBuy, and GovWin](https://www.goveagle.com/integrations) . Each opportunity is checked against your company profile, content library, and current pipeline, then scored with a PWIN from 0 to 100 and the reasoning behind that score. Your team starts the day with a qualified shortlist instead of a raw search feed, and can see why each opportunity made the cut.


For defense work, GovEagle's bid agents also read public solicitations posted to the[Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE)](https://www.goveagle.com/govcon-glossary/piee-procurement-integrated-enterprise-environment) , the DoD procurement system, every day. Those are easy to miss if you only watch SAM.gov. PIEE matches are scored the same way and appear in the same list, with the solicitation type, the contracting office's DoD Activity Address Code (DoDAAC), and the solicitation attachments pulled in.


If discovery is central to your decision, run the same search through both and compare what each surfaces and why.


## Capture management: from research to bid/no-bid


Procurement Sciences describes Awarded AI's capture tools as research agents covering competitors, agencies, and contacts, scored opportunity-fit assessments, and gate reviews tied to the opportunity record. Its materials also describe win themes and competitive insight feeding proposal work.


GovEagle[builds in the capture exercises](https://www.goveagle.com/platform) many teams already run: call planning, a capabilities matrix, and probability of win, with Blue Team and Black Hat reviews forming its gate-review structure. It also has[dedicated Black Hat and Price-to-Win workflows](https://help.goveagle.com/docs/workflows) , so competitive analysis and pricing strategy each get their own working space rather than a notes field.


A lot of capture work also happens in Microsoft Teams. GovEagle can link a Teams channel to an opportunity and save its messages as notes on that opportunity, with who posted, the replies, and a link back to Teams. You can capture every message or only the ones that @mention GovEagle.


Because the notes live on the opportunity, you can ask GovEagle about them later: "What did we decide about the teaming partner last week?"


The difference is one of emphasis. Awarded AI leads with research agents and automated gate assessments; GovEagle leads with the named capture exercises teams already know. Both may support either approach, so see it in the demo.


## Proposals: carrying capture into the response


Both companies say capture intelligence should carry into the proposal. Procurement Sciences describes research, win themes, outlines, compliance checks, drafting, and Red Team reviews. GovEagle[carries capture intelligence into technical approaches, win themes, proposal drafts, and pricing work](https://www.goveagle.com/platform) , alongside RFP shredding, compliance matrices, annotated outlines, and color reviews, including Red Team.


On paper the proposal feature sets are close. What separates them is the handoff: whether a customer priority or competitor insight from capture actually shows up in a proposal section, and whether the pricing lead can see and change the Price-to-Win assumptions behind the number. Ask to see that happen on a real pursuit rather than on a diagram.


## Microsoft Office: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins


Awarded AI has a Microsoft Word add-in for drafting, editing, bulk changes, and evaluator-style comments, and it describes generating a proposal kickoff slide deck.


GovEagle has **add-ins for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint** that work in the file you have open, keeping its structure and styles. Teams can[draft and revise in an existing Word document](https://help.goveagle.com/docs/working-with-the-word-add-in) ,[build and populate compliance or pricing workbooks in Excel](https://help.goveagle.com/docs/working-with-the-excel-add-in) , and[develop capture briefings and orals decks in PowerPoint](https://help.goveagle.com/docs/working-with-the-powerpoint-add-in) .


For visuals, the PowerPoint add-in generates custom slide graphics and drops them into your branded deck, where you can convert them into editable PowerPoint shapes. GovEagle's web app can also[create new Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files from your company templates](https://help.goveagle.com/docs/creating-documents-in-chat) .


GovEagle's custom workflows go a step further. Attach the Word, PowerPoint, or Excel template you want filled in, and each run populates a copy of that file, keeping your layout, instead of producing a generic report you'd have to reformat. The finished document opens in GovEagle for review and editing before you download it. For image sections, you choose between a clean vector diagram and an AI-generated image, and you can edit diagram text in place.


If your compliance matrices and cost models live in Excel and your orals and capture briefings live in PowerPoint, Office support matters as much as drafting. Generating a deck and editing inside PowerPoint are different workflows, so test them separately.


At enterprise scale, this is also a rollout question. When hundreds of writers, reviewers, and pricing analysts keep working in the Word shells, Excel matrices, and branded PowerPoint templates they already use, adopting the platform means adding a tool, not retraining everyone on a new editor.


## CRM integration: keep yours, replace it, or both?


Awarded AI includes a lightweight CRM and says it can replace an existing CRM for many teams, while also integrating with Salesforce. GovEagle[integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Technomile](https://www.goveagle.com/integrations) and is built to work alongside the system your pipeline already lives in.


Get GovCon capture and proposal insights in your inbox.


## SharePoint integration and permissions across business units


For a contractor with several business units, the SharePoint question is really about separation: can the civilian team see the defense team's past performance, and who can open the pricing files?


Both platforms connect to SharePoint. Awarded AI describes selecting permitted sites and folders for synchronization, and also connects to Google Drive. GovEagle offers an[“Inherited from SharePoint” permission mode](https://help.goveagle.com/v1/docs/connecting-sharepoint) that mirrors each user's existing SharePoint access inside GovEagle, so people see only the connected content they're already authorized to see.


That mode requires Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on for the same tenant, certificate authentication, and additional Microsoft Graph permissions; it's a configuration choice, not the default for every connection. For an enterprise, it means GovEagle follows the separation between business units, programs, and pricing data that IT has already set up in SharePoint, rather than asking an administrator to rebuild those rules in a second system.


## FedRAMP certification and data security


Both companies describe[FedRAMP Moderate status](https://www.goveagle.com/security) (the program now calls this certification rather than authorization) and say customer content isn't used to train AI models.


Since the headline claims match, the diligence is in the details, especially if your teams handle[CUI](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/cui-government-contractors-compliance-guide) or need to map AI tools to[NIST 800-171](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/nist-800-171-ai-tools-fedramp-cmmc) : which specific service, deployment, integrations, and data flows are in scope for *your* team and its contractual requirements. Ask each vendor for current authorization details and security documentation for the configuration you would buy.


## Deployment options and IT review


For an enterprise, the security conversation doesn't end at FedRAMP. Your IT and security teams will want to know where the platform runs, who holds the keys, and how access is managed across business units.


GovEagle offers[three deployment models](https://www.goveagle.com/security) : its FedRAMP Certified SaaS, which is the fastest to stand up; a deployment inside your own AWS GovCloud or Azure Government environment, with your own encryption keys, your existing identity and access management, and a dedicated infrastructure option; and air-gapped or on-premise deployments for classified or highly restricted programs, with no internet connection required.


Every user signs in with enforced multi-factor authentication and SSO through Microsoft Entra, Okta, and other providers, and the hosted service carries a 99.9% uptime SLA with multi-region failover.


According to its website, Procurement Sciences runs Awarded AI in single-tenant Azure environments for each customer, offers commercial, government, and self-hosted options (including network-isolated self-hosting), lists GovCloud options, and holds SOC 2 Type 2.


Both vendors offer more than a single shared cloud, so the useful comparison is specific. Ask each one which deployment model your programs would need, who manages the encryption keys in that model, what the uptime commitment is in writing, and how a departing employee's access is removed across every connected system.


## Demo checklist: what each stakeholder should ask for


Enterprise evaluations involve several teams, and each one is testing something different. Give both vendors the same list and the same materials.


**Capture and business development**


1. Use one real services opportunity and show how source material becomes a bid/no-bid recommendation, with citations and editable assumptions.
2. Walk through a Black Hat exercise, including how competitor findings affect win themes and the proposal narrative.
3. Show a DoD solicitation posted to PIEE appearing in the same scored list as SAM.gov opportunities.


**Pricing**


1. Take a Price-to-Win analysis into a cost-volume discussion, showing the assumptions the pricing team can inspect and revise.


**Proposal operations**


1. Populate our existing Excel compliance template and Word proposal shell. Then work in our PowerPoint briefing template, create one custom visual, and show what remains editable.
2. Run a workflow that fills in our own Word, PowerPoint, or Excel template and show the finished file.


**BD operations and CRM**


1. Pull account and opportunity context from our CRM, then show how capture knowledge reaches the proposal team when the solicitation drops.


**IT and security**


1. Connect a SharePoint library and show how inherited permissions and later access changes are enforced for two users with different rights.
2. Walk our security team through the authorization boundary for the configuration we would buy, including every integration we plan to connect.
3. Show SSO setup, role assignment across business units, and how a departing user's access is removed.


## Rollout and procurement checklist


Before signing, enterprise teams should get the same answers from both vendors:


- **Customer support.** Who your team calls when a deadline is at risk, how fast they respond, and whether you get a named contact who knows your account and your pursuits.
- **Getting your team to use it.** How the vendor trains capture managers, writers, reviewers, and pricing analysts, what help is available after launch, and how you'll know people are actually using the platform on live pursuits rather than going back to old habits.
- **Time to first live pursuit.** How long from contract signature to a real proposal running in the platform, including SSO, SharePoint, and CRM connections.
- **Security documentation.** The authorization package, SSP or equivalent, and any third-party reports your security team needs, for the exact configuration you would buy.
- **Integration ownership.** Who sets up and maintains each connection, and what happens to them when the vendor ships an update.
- **Contract terms.** Pricing model as seats and business units grow, data return and deletion at the end of the contract, and the uptime commitment in writing.
- **The business case.** How you'll measure the return. Our guides to[making the BD software business case](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/justify-bd-software-investment-govcon) and[measuring BD tool ROI](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/business-development-tool-roi-government-contractors) cover what finance teams typically ask for, and our[ROI calculator](https://www.goveagle.com/roi-calculator) gives a starting estimate.


For more on evaluating platforms at scale, see our roundup of[enterprise proposal automation platforms for large GovCons](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/enterprise-proposal-automation-platforms-large-govcons) and our[FY 2027 action plan for enterprise GovCon teams](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/fy-action-plan-enterprise-govcon) .


## Which platform fits your team?


GovEagle is a strong fit for teams that want daily, pre-qualified opportunities with a PWIN score they can interrogate, named capture workflows with a built-in Price-to-Win exercise, **Word, Excel, and PowerPoint add-ins and workflows that work in their existing templates** , DoD opportunities from PIEE in the same scored list, and Teams conversations saved to the opportunity, all alongside the CRM they already use.


Awarded AI is worth evaluating for teams drawn to its research agents, the HigherGov market-intelligence portfolio, a built-in pursuit CRM, and its proposal workflow. The clearest answer will come from watching each platform complete the same pursuit tasks with your own materials.


## FAQs


### What is Procurement Sciences AI?


Procurement Sciences is a software company for government contractors, and Awarded AI is its AI platform. Awarded AI covers bid search and matching, capture research, bid/no-bid analysis, and proposal drafting and reviews. Procurement Sciences also owns HigherGov, a market-intelligence product it acquired in May 2026 that continues to run separately.


### Is Awarded AI the same as Procurement Sciences?


No. Procurement Sciences is the company, and Awarded AI is its product. When buyers search for "Procurement Sciences AI," they're usually looking for Awarded AI.


### What is the main difference between GovEagle and Awarded AI?


Both cover business development, capture, and proposals. The clearest differences are in how work gets done: GovEagle has add-ins for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint and workflows that fill in your own templates, qualifies opportunities daily (including DoD solicitations from PIEE) with a PWIN score and its reasoning, saves Teams conversations to the opportunity, and integrates with the CRM you already use. Awarded AI has a Word add-in, leads with research agents and automated gate assessments, and includes its own lightweight CRM.


### Are GovEagle and Awarded AI FedRAMP certified?


Both companies describe FedRAMP Moderate status (now called certification) and say customer content isn't used to train AI models. Ask each vendor for current certification details for the specific deployment and integrations you would use.


### Is there a Procurement Sciences alternative for teams that work in Microsoft Office?


GovEagle is built for teams whose proposals, compliance matrices, cost models, and briefings live in Office. Its add-ins work inside your existing Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files and templates, and it connects to SharePoint, Salesforce, HubSpot, and Technomile.


*Procurement Sciences and Awarded AI are names of their respective owners. GovEagle is not affiliated with or endorsed by Procurement Sciences.*
